summary.text: 国 means “country” or “nation.” It is a simplified form of 國, whose traditional structure combines 囗, marking territory, with 或 as a sound element. In 国, 玉 occupies 或’s position; the history of that replacement is unclear.

formation.text: The traditional graph 國 is phonosemantic: 囗 contributes the territory meaning, and 或 supplies a sound cue. The curated Western Zhou bronze-style image shows an angular inner element within an enclosure; it is a modern redraw illustrating the structure, not an artifact or a sequence of forms. The current graph 国 has 玉 in place of 或, but the reason and pathway for this graphic change are unclear.

components.text: In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory. Some Warring States forms are reported with 匚 or 𠃊 in the same boundary-marker role. This component belongs to 國, the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
In 國, 或 is the phonetic element, but its original depicted referent is not known. 国 has 玉 in the corresponding inner position; the history of this substitution is unclear.

sound_limitation.text: The reconstructions support a sound relationship between 或 and 國 but do not identify 或’s original depicted referent. Modern readings alone do not prove its role in 國.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstructions, 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ are similar but differ in their initial consonant. These are reconstructed forms, not direct records of ancient speech.

components.text: 玉 is the visible inner element in 国, occupying the position of 或 in 國. It is a graphic replacement; the evidence does not show when or why this substitution arose.

history.text: A modern redraw of a Western Zhou bronze-script-style form shows an angular inner element inside an enclosure. It illustrates the reported structure of 國, not an artifact or a proven sequence of graphic stages.

國 with 囗 is reported in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions for “country/state.” Warring States forms may vary the boundary marker; later bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts also use 國 with this meaning. These examples document usage but do not establish a sequence of graphic stages or later meanings.

A Han-dynasty dictionary account analyzes 國 as 囗 plus 或 and glosses it as 邦. The proposed reading of 或 as “country” in the He zun inscription is disputed; another interpretation takes it as 域, “territory.”
国 is reported as simplified from 國, with 玉 in the position of 或, and as the Japanese shinjitai corresponding to 國. The precise pathway and date of this graphic change are unclear.

uncertainties.text: The secure earliest attestation of the word meaning “country/state” remains unsettled: the proposed He zun reading of 或 as 國 is disputed, and the cited research does not include a complete inscription survey.
A dated semantic path from boundary or territory to polity, and the chronology of later senses such as “nation-state,” are not established.
The evidence reports the replacement 或 → 玉 but does not establish its precise historical pathway or why 玉 was selected.

senses.period: Western Zhou inscriptions reported; exact earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions are reported to use 國 for “country/state.” This supports the sense in that period, though the disputed He zun reading of 或 leaves the word’s earliest attestation unsettled.
The character is currently used for “nation” and “country.” The evidence does not date how this range developed from the older country/state sense.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a dated semantic transition from territory or state to the current range “nation, country, nation-state.”

Treasure 或 within a country's borders 囗
Phonosemantic compound. 囗 represents the meaning and 或 represents the sound.
邦也。从囗从或。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kʷɯːɡ): semantic 囗 (“closure”) + phonetic 或 (OC *ɡʷɯːɡ).
The k-prefix derivation of 域 (OC *ɢʷrɯɡ, “boundary; territory”). Cognate with 閾 (OC *qʰʷrɯɡ, “threshold”) and 囿 (OC *ɢʷɯs, *ɡʷɯ, “park; garden”).
No obvious outside cognate exists. It may be related to Burmese ကွက် (kwak, “to be marked with a square or circular pattern; to be confined to a certain area”) (Schuessler, 2007).
邦也。从囗从或。

Etymological analysis: 或 (phonetic)

Bronze 國 combines a territorial enclosure 囗 with phonetic 或. The enclosed form occurs in Western Zhou writing. Earlier 或 could itself write the country or territory word. Some Warring States forms vary the enclosure while retaining its boundary function.
evidence.title: 國 — historical form and meaning

evidence.field: Glyph origin and Japanese form correspondence (English paraphrase)
evidence.text: 国 is a simplified form of 國 with 或 replaced by 玉. It is also the Japanese shinjitai corresponding to 國. The related variant 囯 instead contains 王.
evidence.title: 国 — glyph origin and Japanese forms

evidence.field: 形義通解: 國 graphic structure
evidence.text: The entry analyzes bronze 國 as 囗 plus phonetic 或; 囗 represents a country’s boundary or territory, and the stated original sense is ‘country/state’. Warring States forms may use 匚 or 𠃊 in place of 囗 while retaining a region/boundary marker role.
evidence.title: 國 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 形義通解: early use and semantic attestations
evidence.text: CUHK reports 國 with 囗 in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, used for the country sense, and gives bronze examples from the 彔卣 and 蔡侯鐘. It separately reports 或 used for 國 in bronze inscriptions, citing He zun’s 宅茲中或; one interpretation reads 或 as 國 (‘the middle of the country’), while another takes it as 域 (‘central territory’). The inscription interpretation is disputed in the source. Later examples include Warring States bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts using 國 for country/state, including Mawangdui texts; these attestations document usage but do not establish a sequence of sense extensions.
evidence.title: 國 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi entry as transcribed by CUHK
evidence.text: The transmitted Han-dynasty dictionary account says 國 means 邦 and analyzes it as 从囗从或. This is a historical account and is consistent with, but not independent proof of, the phonetic analysis reported by CUHK.
evidence.title: 國 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: Glyph origin: 國 phonetic series and component analysis
evidence.text: The entry classifies 國 as a phono-semantic compound, semantic 囗 plus phonetic 或. In the Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003 Old Chinese system it lists 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ, alongside multiple members of the same phonetic series; these are reconstructions, not directly attested pronunciations. This supports a phonetic relationship without requiring a claim about the original depicted object, which this research did not establish.
evidence.title: 國 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: For 國, the entry gives modern Standard Mandarin guó (Pinyin) and Guangzhou–Hong Kong Cantonese gwok3 (Jyutping). For 或, it gives modern Beijing huò (Pinyin), Middle Chinese hwok, and Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷˁək in Baxter–Sagart 2014 system 1.1; it also lists Zhengzhang 2003 *ɡʷɯːɡ. The dossier’s 國 metadata separately lists Baxter–Sagart *[C.q]ʷˤək and Zhengzhang *kʷɯːɡ. The within-system Old Chinese reconstructions show similarity with an initial contrast; modern readings are not proof by themselves of the historical sound-component role.
evidence.title: 或 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry identifies 国 as simplified from 國, with 或 replaced by 玉; it also notes unorthodox variant 囯 with 王. It identifies 国 as Japanese shinjitai paired with kyūjitai 國. This is a graphic-form account and does not make 玉 the historical phonetic element of 國.
evidence.title: 国 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: State Council resolution reproduced at Wikisource
evidence.text: The reproduced resolution is dated 28 January 1956 and says first-table simplified characters were to be used from 1 February 1956. The opened page’s first table does not include 国, so this page alone does not date the adoption of 国; it confirms the broader policy context only.
evidence.title: 国务院关于公布汉字简化方案的决议

evidence.field: 形義通解: 國 structure and meanings
evidence.text: The entry describes 國 as bronze-script 囗 plus phonetic 或, with 囗 representing a state's boundary or territory. editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

items.period: Western Zhou (as labeled by the file description)
items.caption: A Western Zhou bronze-script style form of 國 places an angular inner element within a surrounding boundary. The enclosing 囗 marks territory, while the inner 或 serves as the phonetic element.
items.alt: A thick, rounded rectangular enclosure around an angular inner form with several short strokes and a loop.
items.selection_reason: This legible example shows the enclosed 國 structure relevant to the entry’s account of 囗 plus phonetic 或. It is a modern vector redraw, so it illustrates the form rather than serving as an artifact image.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain, as stated on the Wikimedia Commons file page.

limitations.text: The precise referent of the inner 或 form is not established here. A reported early use of 或 for ‘country’ is disputed, so this glyph alone does not settle the earliest attestation of that word.
